title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 184 (Who may be an agent)

content.overview: Section 184 provides that as between the principal and third persons, any person may become an agent, but no person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind can become an agent, so as to be responsible to his principal according to the provisions in that behalf herein contained.
content.glance: As between principal and third persons, any person may be an agent; but only a person of majority age and sound mind can be responsible to the principal under the Act’s provisions.
content.study: As between the principal and third persons, any person may become an agent, but no person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind can become an agent, so as to be responsible to his principal according to the provisions in that behalf herein contained. Current-law framing: broad capacity to act as agent vis-à-vis third persons; limited capacity for responsibility to the principal.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: As between the principal and third persons, any person may become an agent, but no person who is not of the age of majority and of sound mind can become an agent, so as to be responsible to his principal according to the provisions in that behalf herein contained.

examples.title: Any person as agent vis-à-vis third parties
examples.body: As between principal and third persons, any person may act as agent. However, only a major of sound mind can be responsible to the principal under the Act’s provisions, under Section 184.

hypotheticals.question: Can a minor act as an agent so as to bind the principal to third persons?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, as between the principal and third persons. However, the minor cannot be responsible to the principal under the Act’s provisions, under Section 184.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 184
distinctions.body: Section 184 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.
